title: Chat Completions interop mapper: request/response translation for OpenAI CC
creator: Priya Nambiar
description:
Purpose: implement a translator layer that accepts legacy OpenAI Chat Completions (v1/chat/completions) requests and translates them into Redwood’s internal streaming/function-calling/structured-output protocol, then converts runtime responses back into the OpenAI response shape. This enables customers with existing OpenAI integrations to migrate to Redwood with minimal changes to their integration while preserving streaming semantics and tool invocation behavior.

Scope and constraints: translate request fields (model, messages, max_tokens, temperature, top_p, n, stop, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty, user, functions, function_call) into our Serve API call shape. Maintain first-byte streaming and incremental delta events so clients receive tokens in the same cadence they expect from OpenAI streams. Map function/tool schemas into internal tool registry calls with guards for signature mismatch and timeouts. Structured outputs (JSON schemas / assistant payload blocks) must be preserved and verified against declared schema where provided.

Key translation rules (summary):
- messages[] -> conversation array with role normalization: system|user|assistant mapped to internal roles and metadata preserved. Legacy 'name' fields are attached to message metadata.
- n (choices) -> parallel generation requests when n > 1; maintain consistent stream multiplexing with choice identifiers so clients can differentiate choice streams.
- streaming: produce data: events that mimic OpenAI incremental deltas; include token indices, role switches, and tool call begin/complete markers. For our event envelope, we add a compatibility header 'x-compat: openai-chat' but do not expose internal request ids.
- functions + function_call: validate function signatures, map to internal tool IDs, support both explicit 'name' triggers and 'auto' function_call behavior. Tool invocation is converted into a two-phase event stream: a tool_call_start event (with name and input), then a tool_output stream, then tool_call_end. Back-translate into OpenAI's function call fields in the final choices when returning non-streaming responses or emit the equivalent in the last streamed chunk.
- structured output: when messages contain an assistant response that claims to be json/structured, run lightweight schema validation (when functions/schema provided) and emit structured_output field in the compatibility payload. If validation fails, include a 'structured_output_error' in the final choice and include a deterministic fallback plain-text rendering.
- errors/timeouts: map internal errors to OpenAI error codes where possible; for tool timeouts return a choice with finish_reason: "tool_timeout" and an error object in the compatibility 'error' field.

Trade-offs and design decisions so far:
- We intentionally do not replicate OpenAI's exact event framing byte-for-byte; instead we provide a compat layer that mirrors the semantics (incremental token deltas, choice ids, function call events). This reduces complexity of brittle wire-level compatibility while keeping client expectations intact.
- For performance, when n>1 we will avoid duplicating full KV cache contexts by reusing a shared prefix cache and spawning incremental continuations; this requires careful concurrency controls.
- We will not attempt to emulate deprecated OpenAI fields (e.g., logprobs) beyond adding a placeholder structure flagged as unsupported to avoid surprising customers.

Implementation plan (high-level):
1) Define translation library (go module) with deterministic mappings and a test vector corpus covering the top 50 real-world CC integrations.
2) Instrument runtime to emit compatibility stream events and add x-compat header.
3) Add function/tool signature adapter that verifies and registers temporary shim wrappers for incoming functions; implement sandboxed invocation path.
4) Update SDKs with docs and sample code showing how to switch endpoints and toggles.
5) Canary rollout: 2% traffic -> 10% -> 25% -> 100% with canary metrics and automatic rollback on error budget burn.

Acceptance criteria and tests:
- End-to-end tests that replay 500 saved OpenAI CC sessions and assert client-visible fields match expected sequence (tokens, function_call events, final choices) within tolerance for interleaving.
- Streaming latency SLO: 95th percentile first token < 150ms for small prompts on Dedicated pools.
- No silent schema drop: whenever a structured output schema is declared, the final compatibility response must include either validated structured_output or a clear structured_output_error.
- Telemetry: emit mapping events for each translated request with fields: compat_version, mapping_path, function_invocations.

Rollout plan and toggles: initially gate the feature behind a per-customer toggle (compat_oai_chat_v1). Add opt-in via Console per project and a global feature flag for internal QA. Canary metrics include error rate, tool_timeout rate, structured_output_validation_fail_rate, and end-to-end latency.

Open questions / blockers:
- How to represent multi-choice streaming to clients that expect a single combined stream? (Proposal: keep separate choice streams but add a combined final choice in the non-streaming endpoint for parity).
- Sandbox limits for function calls (cpu/time) - need SRE guidance and quota knobs.
- Backpressure semantics for tool outputs vs. token generation: if a tool emits a large payload, should we chunk it as tokens or as a distinct tool_output stream?

Links and artifacts: design doc, test corpus, and prototype PRs listed below.

Note: see comments for incremental updates and reviewer feedback.

2026-03-08 Jake Morrison (Backend Eng): Prototype successfully converts function_call events and streams tool_call_start/tool_output/tool_call_end. Pushed prototype branch: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serve/pull/7891
2026-03-09 Security review request submitted (sec-ticket SEC-3120) to validate sandboxing model; security requested explicit KMS usage guidance for sensitive tool outputs.

2026-03-11 Liam Carter (Assignee): Implemented basic n>1 parallelization with shared KV prefix; discovered race when cache eviction happens mid-generation. Added mitigation: lock per-session prefix for short critical window. Follow-up: ENG-60210 to refine lock granularity.
2026-03-12 QA: Streaming replay harness broken on windows due to newline framing differences; updated test harness to normalize line endings.
qa_plan: Create a harness that replays recorded OpenAI CC traffic against the compat endpoint. Validate event ordering, token deltas, function_call lifecycle events, and final choice shapes. Run the harness on each canary stage and block rollout if structured_output_validation_fail_rate > 0.5% or error rate doubles baseline.
acceptance_criteria: 1) 500/500 recorded sessions pass event-sequence checks in CI. 2) Streaming latency within SLO on canary. 3) No high-severity security findings after sandbox review. 4) Console toggle and SDK samples published.
notes: This ticket avoids deep wire-level byte parity with OpenAI. Focus is developer-visible semantics. Keep the translation library small, well-instrumented, and test-vector-driven. After initial launch we'll consider beta support for legacy fields if customers request them.
